explanation: N521+ fires on the predicate word of a clause - the verb, predicative adjective or focused adverb that carries the assertion - and a subordinating opener multiplies its strength several-fold: 'if you want' 0.75 vs 'So you want' 0.00, 'when you want' 0.58 vs 'while you want' 0.10, 'whether you want' 0.65 vs 'although you want' 0.11, 'if I did' 1.13 vs 'since I did' 0.67, 'if you have questions' 1.34 vs the same without 'if' 0.62, 'until now' 1.06 vs 'until then' 0.77, against 0.0-0.2 for the subordinator itself, for determiners/prepositions/auxiliaries, for later content words of the same clause ('if you want to make shopping economic': 'make'/'shopping'/'economic' all 0.00), for ordinary noun objects in plain declaratives ('He bought the hat/lawyer/car yesterday' 0.00), and for the same verb when the clause opens with So/And/While/Although/After (0.00-0.10). Without any subordinator it still fires at 0.4-1.4 on a small intrinsic-propensity set of predicate words ('had been dominant' 1.16, 'is critical' 0.97, 'particularly difficult' 1.23, 'In return' 0.78), so its strongest peaks need both factors.
